action: Traefik says it strongly recommends upgrading as soon as possible to 2.11.64, 3.7.20 or 3.8.0; v3.6 and earlier v3 releases get no patch, so move them to 3.7.20 or 3.8.0.
date_note: Date of Traefik's security announcement; Sempre Update says the releases came out on 23 November.
exec: Traefik has patched a High-severity memory-exhaustion flaw and two Medium-severity flaws in its reverse proxy; the post does not say whether any is exploited.
plain: The Traefik reverse proxy has updates fixing three security flaws: one lets unauthenticated clients exhaust memory, one can leak credentials into debug logs, and one can let a router take over a host protected by client-certificate TLS.
summary: Traefik's announcement lists three advisories fixed in 2.11.64, 3.7.20 and 3.8.0. GHSA-3rh5-223h-cpwr (High) lets unauthenticated clients exhaust memory through Brotli compression in the Compress middleware; GHSA-42x2-976f-ph52 (Medium) exposes Docker/Swarm passwords, Knative tokens and HTTP provider headers in debug logs; GHSA-9657-c2gv-wjpj (Medium) lets a trailing-dot host router take over a client-certificate-protected host. The post does not state whether any is exploited.
title: Traefik patches Brotli memory-exhaustion, debug-log credential exposure and TLS option flaws

validation.note: Vendor announcement (Traefik community post) read, plus Sempre Update; primary source.
